derivation: The gasoline-gallon-equivalent basis the EPA fuel-economy label uses for fuel-cell vehicles (1 kg H2 = 1 gge = 33.7 kWh), so the label's kWh/100 mi is the energy content of the hydrogen burned. The Korean label publishes km per kg and is converted on the same basis, putting both markets' certified values on one scale.

IRENA (2020), Green hydrogen cost reduction, note to figure on p.11: an alkaline electrolyser at nominal capacity is 65% efficient, an LHV of 51.2 kWh per kg of hydrogen in 2020. Station compression to 700 bar, storage and delivery are NOT included, so the electricity drawn per kilometre is a floor and the fuel-cell result understates its own emissions.
